text: This is an accelerated brush study, with colors sampled from the reference.
The reference is not imported as artwork; native brush marks build five stages.
Stage one lays in broad masses with a large Oils preset.
Separate bouquet and background, using black wrapping to support the red blooms.
Stage two establishes the main shadows and lit planes.
Read the large value relationships before describing individual petals.
Observe alternating cool and warm reds to separate the flower masses.
This sampled-color study shows marks accumulating, not real-time manual footage.
Stage three uses smaller marks to recover turns in foliage and wrapping.
Oil and Dry brush brushes leave different edges to distinguish the forms.
The impasto impression comes from arranged masses and directional marks.
This is not a three-dimensional paint simulation; values and edges do the work.
Stage four refines petals, reserving detail for the main roses.
Keep shadows simple; a few clear lit planes can describe the petals.
Compare this stage with the block-in before deciding how much to resolve.
Leave some edges unresolved so the painting retains quiet passages.
The last stage adds pale flowers and highlights, then checks the overall hierarchy.
The study canvas consists of real brush marks and is shown separately from the reference.
